description: Bounded relational verification cases. Each declares its expected outcome, so a compiler change that invalidates one surfaces as an unmet expectation rather than being absorbed. Expectations are never used to decide the outcome.

cases.description: secret-indexed load: the secret selects a memory address
cases.rationale: the instruction sequence is identical for every secret, so only an address-aware analysis can see this; M1's instruction-path comparison cannot

cases.description: secret-dependent loop trip count: a branch that survives optimization
cases.rationale: a secret-dependent `if` returning constants is if-converted into arithmetic, but a loop's backward conditional jump cannot be

cases.description: constant-time full-table scan with mask selection
cases.rationale: reads every entry and selects without a secret-dependent branch or address; exploration completes, so the bounded property is established over the declared domain

cases.description: branches on a public input only, with the secret used in arithmetic
cases.rationale: both compared executions share the public input, so public-dependent branching is not a leak; this pins that down rather than assuming it

cases.description: a leak reachable only under one public mode
cases.rationale: the milestone's key demonstration: a dynamic test exercising only public==0 observes nothing, because that path is the masked scan. Finding this needs a search over the public domain, not a chosen input

cases.description: educational: a source-level secret branch the compiler removed
cases.rationale: at -O this compiles to shr plus sub with zero conditional jumps, so the honest verdict is that the compiled code has no secret-dependent control flow. Declared VERIFIED_BOUNDED rather than manufacturing a leak -- the fourth instance of compiler branch-erasure recorded in this project

cases.description: deliberately exceeds a small exploration bound
cases.rationale: a public-bounded loop against max_depth 40 leaves paths unexplored; the analyzer reports unknown and total paths exceed completed ones, so a clean verdict must not be issued
